About Event
​🧠 Cognee, AWS Strands Agent, Docker Sandbox, Bright Data

​$100 in credits for everyone. $1000 in prizes for the winners!

​Join us for Battle of the Personal Brains, a 5 hour hands-on AI hackathon where you’ll build an intelligent personal agent powered by your own data, live information, and create an agentic workflow to take action, all under one roof at the Bright Data office in SOMA.

​Build the personal AI agent you’ve always wanted.

​In today’s world, it’s possible for an AI agent to know what you know - your emails, your documents, meetings, calendar, tasks, files, and other information that’s relevant to you - and then act on it.

​For this hackathon, the challenge is simple: Build a brain. Build an agent. Then make it do something.

​​🗓️ Event Details

​When: 4:00 PM – 9:00 PM, Monday September 21, 2026

​Where: Bright Data office, San Francisco, CA

​🧠 First, Build your Personal Brain

​Your agent is only as useful as the information it can understand. So you’ll create an AI-powered brain that can combine knowledge from multiple sources:

​Your laptop and local files

​Google Drive and cloud documents

​Personal email and other data sources

​Public information from across the web

​Meeting notes, receipts, photos, schedules, and more

​You'll use Cognee’s structured AI memory to create your Personal Brain, and Bright Data to discover and retrieve public web data.

​🤖 Then, Build your Agent

​Once your agent can access the right knowledge, the real fun begins. Build an agent that can find information, reason across it, and take action.

​Your agent could:

​Manage your calendar - Find availability and schedule an appointment automatically.

​Take notes and remind you later - Capture information and send a reminder exactly when you need it.

​Turn meetings into action - Read meeting summaries, identify commitments and action items, and build your personal to-do schedule.

​Handle your expenses - Process receipts, extract the important information, organize them, and prepare expense reports.

​Organize and share your photos - Process photos, upload them to Google Photos, organize them, and share them with your WhatsApp group.

​Build your own personal assistant - Create an agent that understands your information, remembers what's important, and helps you get things done.

​Connect your digital life - Connect to apps and services you use every day, read through information, create notes, identify what matters, and remind you when action is required.

​Or build something completely different.

​Your brain. Your agent. Your idea.

​🛠️ The Agentic Stack

​We'll provide technologies you can combine to build your agent:

​🧠 Cognee — The Brain - Create long-term AI memory and a Personal Brain that your agent can search, understand, and reason over. Get $50 of Cognee Cloud Credits.

​🌐 Bright Data — The Web - Give your agent access to fresh public information from across the web. Get $50 of Bright Data Credits.

​📁 Your Data — The Personal Brain - Bring your own files and information from your laptop, Google Drive, and other sources.

​🤖 AWS Strands Agents — The Agent Harness - Build and orchestrate the agent that reasons, uses tools, and decides what to do next.

​🐳 Docker Sandboxes — The Sandbox - Give your agent a secure environment where it can run code and perform tasks.

​Together, these technologies give your agent something increasingly important:

​Data + Memory + Reasoning + Tools + Actions

​⚔️ The Battle

​This isn't just about building another chatbot. We're looking for agents that can understand information and then accomplish something useful.

​At the end of the hackathon, each team will demonstrate what their agents can do. Will it remember better? Find better information? Reason across personal, company, and public data? Can it take useful actions?

​But most importantly: Can your brain beat the other brains?

​👩‍💻 Who Should Attend?

​Developers, AI engineers, agent builders, hackers, founders, students, and anyone interested in building the next generation of personal AI agents. You don't need to arrive with a finished idea. Come with a laptop, some curiosity, and a problem you'd love an AI agent to solve. We'll help you build the rest.

​👩‍💻 What to Expect?

​$100 free credits ($50 from Cognee + $50 from Bright Data)

​$1000 in prizes for the top 3 winners! $500, $300, $200

​High-Energy Building Sessions: 5 hours to prototype cutting-edge data and agentic workflows

​Data & AI Challenges: Solve real-world problems that you and others can benefit from

​Expert Mentorship: On-site guidance from developer advocates from Cognee, AWS and Bright Data.

​Swag, Catering & Networking: Fuel up with snacks and food while connecting with fellow builders and founders.

​Prizes & Demos: Win prizes and pitch your build directly to industry leaders.

​🚀 What You'll Leave With

​By the end of the hackathon, you'll have gone beyond prompts and chatbots. You'll have built an agent with:

​A brain that remembers.

​Knowledge it can retrieve.

​Tools it can use.

​And the ability to take action.

​Welcome to the Battle of the Personal Brains.

​🧠 Build your brain. Build your agent. Enter the battle.

​Event Terms & Consent

​By registering, you agree to the event terms and conditions. Cognee reserves the right to refuse admission or remove attendees at its discretion to keep things safe and enjoyable for everyone.

​Photography and video recording will take place throughout the evening and may be used by Cognee and Bright Data for future marketing, promotional, and community content. By registering, you also consent to receiving the Cognee newsletter and updates about future events at the email address you provide. You can unsubscribe anytime via the link in any email.

​Spots are limited. Register now and build the future of Personal Brains.

WHAT IS re:AGENT

re:AGENT is a two-day build weekend focused on the infrastructure scientific agents still need: better datasets, sharper tools, and reliable ways to evaluate their work. Participants will use Paperclip , Proto , Claude , and other scientific AI tools to build systems that can take on real scientific problems and produce results worth trusting.
Paperclip turns papers, datasets, clinical trials, and biological databases into an agent-native workspace that AI systems can search, synthesize, and build upon. Proto is a design framework and infrastructure layer for generative biology, allowing builders to combine AI models and search for DNA, RNA, or protein sequences that satisfy custom criteria.
The weekend brings together engineers, scientists, computational biologists, founders, and AI researchers. Projects might include assembling a research-ready dataset that would be impractical to create by hand, along with the analysis needed to show that its findings are real. Others might involve designing a new biological system to a defined specification and testing whether it holds up against existing evidence.
The aim is not just to accelerate existing workflows, but to create the tools, datasets, and evaluation methods that make entirely new scientific questions and experiments possible.

Track A: Build an AI Scientist
Build an AI agent that can carry out a defined scientific or drug-development workflow from start to finish. It should gather evidence, use relevant tools or databases, generate and test hypotheses, produce a structured output, and make its reasoning easy to inspect. This could mean reasoning over experimental data, scientific literature, or learned representations like protein embeddings. Examples include a virtual FDA reviewer, toxicology agent, clinical trial designer, experimental planning agent, or a protein-discovery agent that generates and tests hypotheses over protein embeddings and structural features.

🧬 Care Delivery & Clinical Innovation
Build AI that makes care more accessible, personalized, and effective , from diagnostics and specialty care to home-based care, clinical trials, robotics, and entirely new models of care delivery.

🏥 Healthcare Infrastructure & Financing
Build AI that fixes the systems behind healthcare , improving how care is financed, administered, coordinated, and delivered across providers, payers, employers, marketplaces, and supply chains.

🔬 AI × Life Sciences
Build AI that better predicts what will actually happen in biology , using richer, multi-compartment data to model real-world outcomes such as toxicity, delivery, efficacy, and clinical trial endpoints rather than focusing only on molecular binding.

About Event

What are we doing?!
We're taking over DG717 for one Sunday and turning the entire ground floor into an AI filmmaking lab.
Here's the format. There are hundreds of manga books sitting inside the space. You walk in, pick a book, pick a chapter, and you have three hours to turn it into an AI film. Any tool you want. Image gen, video gen, voice, music, sound, editing, whatever gets you there.
This is not a hackathon where people sit around building software. It's a room full of creative people, a great piece of source material, and the best AI filmmaking tools available, for three hours.
At the end, we screen every film. And we pick the best one.
The winning team gets a one month opportunity to work with Kodansha USA .
What to expect
A full manga library set up and ready to go

A hard three hour clock, from pick to final cut

Bring a laptop

A live screening the moment the clock runs out

A shot at a one month collab with Kodansha USA

P.S: this isn't for total beginners. If you've spent real time in Midjourney, Runway, Kling, Veo, or ElevenLabs, this is for you.
If you haven't but you have taste, apply anyway.
The day
11:30 AM: Arrival Food, coffee, drinks. Meet the other filmmakers before the clock starts. The manga library is already set up, come early and start browsing.
12:00 PM: Competition starts Pick your manga. Pick your chapter or scene. The second you pick it, your three hours begin.
12:00 - 3:00 PM: Production Every participant gets a desk, power, and a desk lamp. The ground floor becomes a production floor. Shoot, generate, edit, score, finish.
3:00 PM: Clock stops Submissions close. The space flips from studio to screening room.
3:30 PM: Screening + Awards We watch every film together. Creators talk through what they made and how. Then the jury picks a winner.
What are you actually being judged on?
Not just "does this look cool." We're looking for:
Story : did you pick and interpret the source material well

Direction : is there a clear point of view here

Visuals : does it look good

Effects : did you use AI to do something that would've been genuinely hard to pull off otherwise

Character : do the characters hold together across the film

Sound : does the music, voice, and sound design earn their place

Editing : is the pacing right

Originality : did you do something interesting with the source, not just the obvious take

And the real question underneath all of it: does it actually feel like a film?
We're not trying to find whoever can generate the single coolest shot. We're trying to find whoever can use these tools to tell the best story.
The vibe
Think Japanese design meets manga meets Tokyo meets AI meets cinema. Paper, typography, lighting, desk lamps, screens, projections. Walk in and you should immediately know this isn't a normal hackathon. It should feel like a Japanese creative studio, dropped into the future.
Getting in
Spots are limited to keep the room small and the work good. Apply through this page and we'll follow up with the details once you're confirmed.
Who's behind this
LocalhostHQ runs media and tech labs around the world, spaces where filmmakers, technologists, and designers come together to make things that push culture forward.
DG717 / Digital Garage is hosting us in San Francisco, bringing decades of Japanese innovation history into the room.

About Event

Build It. Test It. Prove It.
Smells like a hackathon. Runs like a pressure test, on you, not just your idea.
Proving Ground runs a three-day Sprint where judges push past the pitch. No script survives real questions about what you tried, what broke, and what you changed.
Past teams have gone on to raise from 500 Global and Blitzscaling Ventures, and been accepted into Berkeley SkyDeck and Confluent's accelerator, independently, without Proving Ground's involvement in those decisions.
What this is
A hackathon judges what you built by the end. We watch during the process and look past the end to what may come next.

The team is almost everything. How you make decisions under pressure, how you handle a setback, how you treat each other when something breaks. You'll document that as you go. What we ask you to show and how we question it are built around behavior, not performance.
How it works
Over three days, founders build under real constraint. No script, no rehearsed demo. Judges probe what you tried, what broke, and what you changed, and compare where you started to where you ended.
Two Tracks
Discovery Track. Pre-market, no active customer contact yet. For the startup curious, including enterprise folks seriously exploring a leap.
Pre-seed Track. In-market, already talking to customers. Ship something real, show what's changed, pressure-test your next move.
After the Sprint
Select teams get invited into the Street Test: 30 days back in the real world, no artificial deadline, no audience. This is where we see if momentum was real or borrowed from the room. It's the part a hackathon can't offer, because a hackathon ends when the weekend does.

About Event

The Lowdown 👋
One year ago, we opened a hub where AI builders could show up for each other. On September 22, we're celebrating everyone who did — and everything that got built because of it!
Join us for a night of real conversations about AI, community, and what comes next. We will have:
A panel with AI builders, community leaders, and founders moderated by Jeremiah Owyang

Builders who came here for a hackathon weekend and are still shipping

Stories from startups who built their companies right inside these walls

Plus food, music, a photo booth, community trading cards, and more!

The SVAI Hub was built on one conviction: the best AI doesn't get built in isolation. It gets built by communities — developers leveling up together, founders stress-testing ideas with peers, researchers colliding with practitioners in the same room. In September 2025, we opened our space in the heart of Silicon Valley. Not for vendor pitches. Not for product demos. For the conversations and connections that actually move the field forward.
One year in, the numbers tell part of the story:
100+ AI community events

10,000+ developers, founders, and executives through our doors

6 hackathons that launched real projects and real careers

The numbers tell part of the story. The conversations tell the rest.
Come for the milestone. Stay for the momentum, connections and networking!
Registration requires approval and space is limited. If this sounds like your room, request your spot now!
The Humans at the Mic 🎤
Built Here. Still Building. — Hackathon Winners Spotlight
Victoria Duan — OrchestrAI | Llama Lounge Hackathon, 1st Place
Victoria built the core agentic framework for OrchestrAI, took first place, and hasn't stopped building since — she's now deep in AI developer tooling and exploring how AI changes the way software gets made.

Abraham Bhatti , Rishit Sai & Yash Sanghvi — ToolForge | Llama Lounge Hackathon, 2nd Place
They built an AI agent that creates its own tools, won together, kept competing together, and are now in early customer discovery to turn it into a real product.

Panel: Build Together — The Advantage of Community in AI
Jeremiah Owyang (moderator) — VC at Blitzscaling Ventures, global keynote speaker, and founder of Llama Lounge — the Bay Area's most popular AI startup event series, drawing hundreds of founders, investors, and builders every month.

Grace Gong — Founder of Smart Venture Media, host of two top-ranked VC podcasts (Smart Venture Podcast and Venture with Grace), angel investor, and founder of Smart AI Summits — a LinkedIn Top Voice in Finance with a front-row seat to where AI and venture capital intersect.

Swagata Ashwani — AI Tech Lead & Manager at Boomi, co-lead of the Women in Data SF chapter, and a LinkedIn Top Voice in AI — a technical builder who brings a practitioner's view of how community helps people stay sharp, learn faster, and grow with AI.

Sheena Tu — Co-founder of TechEquity Ai, a Silicon Valley nonprofit expanding access to AI through practical learning, industry collaboration, and community-driven programs, including forums, workshops, hackathons, and its annual Summit, reaching thousands of participants across the Bay Area and beyond.

Startup Showcase — Stories from the Hub
Every week, a group of startup founders work from the SVAI Hub. Two of those companies will share what they're building, how this community changed how they built it, and where they are now — in three minutes, no pitch deck.
Ivan Lee — Founder and CEO, Datasaur
Ivan sold his first startup to Yahoo, built AI systems at Apple, and has spent the last seven years focused on the problem most AI vendors don't want to talk about: what happens to your data after you hand it over. At Datasaur, he helps enterprises in financial services, healthcare, legal, and government deploy fully air-gapped private LLMs — frontier-model capability, zero data leaving the building. His version of the future: the most powerful AI is the one you fully control.

Mayank Kumar — Founding AI Engineer, DeepTempo
Over the last decade Mayank has built safety-critical systems, trained large-scale AI models, and served communities through his social entrepreneurial ventures. At DeepTempo, he is building the Intelligent Defense Platform. Attackers are already using AI to move faster than the teams defending against them, and those teams are working with tools built for a slower era. The platform is his answer to that gap: LogLM is the intelligence layer, a foundation model that learns what normal activity looks like across many kinds of security data and flags what does not belong, and Vigil is the investigation layer, an open source system where AI agents take those signals and work out what actually happened. His bet for the next few years: defenders need to operate at machine speed too.

The Rundown 🗓️
5:00 PM: Doors open. Grab some food and drinks, hit the photo booth, and make your own trading card
5:30 PM: Welcome and Year in Review
5:45 PM: Built Here. Still Building. — Hackathon builder spotlights
6:00 PM: Panel: Build Together — The Advantage of Community in AI
6:30 PM: Startup Showcase — Stories from the Hub
6:40 PM: Closing remarks and community toast
6:45 PM: Open networking, happy hour, and community booths until 8:00 PM
Is This Your Crowd? 👀
This event is designed for the AI community — and that means all of it. If you are an engineer or developer actively building with AI, a researcher pushing the field forward, a founder scaling an AI startup, or an executive figuring out where AI fits in your organization's future, you will find the conversations and the people in the room directly relevant. We also welcome those who are earlier in the journey — someone looking to break into AI, learn from practitioners, or understand what is actually happening beyond the headlines.
Whether you are shipping AI products in production, growing a company you started at a hackathon, running community programs that bring builders together, or just getting serious about AI for the first time — this is a room for people who believe the best AI gets built by people who show up for each other.

About Event

" The way to get startup ideas is not to try to think of startup ideas. It's to look for problems, preferably problems you have yourself." Paul Graham
Most people who want to build something sit in a room and brainstorm ideas. That is the wrong starting point.
The right starting point is a real problem. That is the ITCH worth scratching.
If you do not have that problem yourself, come find it here.

ITCH is a panel discussion with business owners or industry experts in the SF community. We dig into what is actually hard in their business right now. Together, we find the ITCH .
You leave with a list of real problems you can actually work on. And some of the panelists might let you pilot your solution with them directly.

You can find ways to leverage AI for these problems.
